policy.source_role: EGP and GSE Grammar are evidence inventories, not automatic lesson or mastery checklists.
policy.course_item_role: The controlled items define exact A1 forms, meanings, limits, contexts, and fresh-task mastery evidence.
policy.ownership_status: Candidate owners are reconciliation contexts and may move intact when candidates merge or the final sequence changes.
policy.variety_policy: Internationally intelligible core English is taught; have is the course default while BrE have got is registered as valid.
policy.assessment_policy: Grammar is assessed through meaning-preserving use in fresh communicative tasks, not rule naming or isolated recall alone.

course_items.title: Present be: affirmative
exact_forms: subject + be + name, age, nationality, job, location, noun phrase, or adjective
course_items.meaning_use: Identify and describe people, things, states, and locations in the present.
course_items.mastery_evidence: Produce accurate subject-be agreement in fresh identity and description prompts.
course_items.not_yet: Past be and complex complements wait for later control.

course_items.title: Present be: negative
course_items.meaning_use: Correct or deny a present identity, state, description, or location.
course_items.mastery_evidence: Correct a false detail using the matching negative form without a model.
course_items.not_yet: No emphatic, tag, or contrastive negative system at A1.

course_items.title: Present be: questions and short answers
exact_forms: Yes, subject + am/is/are; No, subject + am not/isn't/aren't
course_items.meaning_use: Ask and answer direct questions about identity, state, description, and location.
course_items.mastery_evidence: Complete a fresh information gap with correct be-question order and relevant short answers.
course_items.not_yet: Embedded questions and question tags wait for later levels.

course_items.title: Present simple: affirmative
exact_forms: limited irregular forms: have/has, do/does, go/goes
course_items.meaning_use: State present facts, routines, likes, and familiar repeated actions.
course_items.mastery_evidence: Write or say fresh facts about self and another person with controlled third-person agreement.
course_items.not_yet: Subtle stative/dynamic distinctions and broader irregular morphology wait.

course_items.title: Present simple: negative
course_items.meaning_use: State that a fact, preference, possession, or routine is not true.
course_items.mastery_evidence: Correct false routine and preference statements using do/does plus the base verb.
course_items.not_yet: Negative adverbials and emphatic do wait for later levels.

course_items.title: Present simple: questions and short answers
exact_forms: Yes, subject + do/does; No, subject + don't/doesn't
course_items.meaning_use: Exchange facts, routines, possessions, likes, and wants.
course_items.mastery_evidence: Ask and answer fresh yes/no and wh- questions without retaining -s on the main verb after does.
course_items.not_yet: Indirect and negative questions wait for later levels.

course_items.title: Basic statement order
course_items.meaning_use: Build short intelligible statements with an explicit subject and stable word order.
course_items.mastery_evidence: Reconstruct fresh short statements and preserve who did or is what.
course_items.not_yet: Inversion, fronting for discourse effect, and complex clause patterns wait.

course_items.title: Subject and object personal pronouns
exact_forms: subjects: I, you, he, she, it, we, they
objects: me, you, him, her, it, us, them
object pronoun after a verb or preposition
course_items.meaning_use: Keep reference clear when talking about people and familiar things.
course_items.mastery_evidence: Replace fresh noun phrases with the correct subject or object pronoun in context.
course_items.not_yet: Generic, reflexive, and reciprocal pronouns wait.

course_items.title: Possessive determiners and singular 's
exact_forms: my, your, his, her, its, our, their + noun
course_items.meaning_use: Show familiar ownership and personal relationships.
course_items.mastery_evidence: Identify and express who a fresh familiar person or object belongs to.
course_items.not_yet: Independent possessive pronouns and plural possessive apostrophes wait.

course_items.title: Present continuous: actions now
exact_forms: receptive recognition of present negative and question forms
course_items.meaning_use: Describe a visible or immediate action in progress and distinguish it from a routine.
course_items.mastery_evidence: Choose present simple for a routine and present continuous for a pictured action, then produce one accurate action-now statement.
course_items.not_yet: Future arrangement use and a broad spelling-rule inventory wait for A2.

course_items.title: Past simple: limited familiar events
exact_forms: affirmative with was/were and a bounded set such as went, had, liked, worked, lived
course_items.meaning_use: State one or two completed familiar past events or states when time is clear.
course_items.mastery_evidence: After a fresh visual sequence, produce two controlled past facts, including one negative contrast.
course_items.not_yet: Past questions, narrative expansion, and a broad irregular-verb inventory wait for A2.

course_items.title: Will/'ll: simple plans and commitments
course_items.meaning_use: State a simple intended action, promise, arrival, or return in a familiar arrangement.
course_items.mastery_evidence: Complete a fresh arrangement or return message with an intended action and time.
course_items.not_yet: Predictions, spontaneous decisions, negative forms, and will-questions wait.

course_items.title: Can/can't: ability and simple possibility
course_items.meaning_use: State present ability or whether a familiar action is possible in the situation.
course_items.mastery_evidence: Exchange fresh ability facts and choose can or can't from the evidence in the task.
course_items.not_yet: Probability meanings and past or future ability wait.

course_items.title: Can: requests and offers
exact_forms: Can I help? / What can I do for you?
course_items.meaning_use: Request an action, offer help, or check a simple shared action politely.
course_items.mastery_evidence: Complete a fresh service or help exchange with a clear can-question and relevant response.
course_items.not_yet: Could/would request scales and nuanced permission wait.

course_items.title: Would like and want: bounded wants
exact_forms: I would/I'd like to + base verb
I would like to invite + person + to + event
course_items.meaning_use: Express a simple want, service choice, preference, or formulaic invitation.
course_items.mastery_evidence: Select and produce the appropriate frame in a fresh order, booking, or invitation prompt.
course_items.not_yet: Would for hypotheticals, habits, and nuanced politeness waits.

course_items.title: Positive and negative imperatives
exact_forms: two or three ordered verb-led steps
course_items.meaning_use: Give or follow direct familiar instructions, warnings, and route steps.
course_items.mastery_evidence: Order and carry out or produce fresh two- or three-step instructions accurately.
course_items.not_yet: Let’s suggestions and complex procedural subordination wait.

course_items.title: There is/are: presence and absence
course_items.meaning_use: State and ask what exists in a room, home, or familiar place.
course_items.mastery_evidence: Complete a fresh room information gap with accurate singular/plural forms.
course_items.not_yet: There has been and presentational there beyond presence wait.

course_items.title: Have/has and have got: possession
exact_forms: recognise and optionally produce BrE have/has got and Have ... got?
course_items.meaning_use: State and exchange family, possession, home, and familiar feature information.
course_items.mastery_evidence: Exchange fresh possession facts using the chosen course default and understand the registered BrE variant.
course_items.not_yet: Perfect have and broader have got idioms wait.

course_items.title: A/an, the, and bounded zero article
exact_forms: zero article with plural/uncount general nouns and fixed at home/by car/go to college
course_items.meaning_use: Mark one nonspecific item, an identifiable item, or a bounded general/fixed expression.
course_items.mastery_evidence: Choose a/an, the, or zero in fresh bounded identity, object, and service phrases.
course_items.not_yet: Full article discourse choice, institutions beyond taught chunks, and generic the wait.

course_items.title: Noun number and basic quantity
exact_forms: common irregular plurals: people, children, women, men
some/a lot of/lots of + plural or uncount noun
course_items.meaning_use: Refer to one or more familiar items and express a useful bounded quantity.
course_items.mastery_evidence: Name and quantify fresh familiar items without singular/plural mismatch.
course_items.not_yet: Productive much/many, fewer/less, and complex partitives wait.

course_items.title: Basic noun-phrase order and roles
exact_forms: adjective + plural noun with no determiner when licensed
noun phrase as subject, object, complement, or preposition complement
course_items.meaning_use: Build compact referents that preserve which person or thing is meant.
course_items.mastery_evidence: Build and place fresh bounded noun phrases correctly inside short statements.
course_items.not_yet: Dense modification, complex determiners, and productive compounding wait.

course_items.title: This: near reference and current time
course_items.meaning_use: Point to a nearby or current referent, introduce someone, or identify the coming time period.
course_items.mastery_evidence: Use this with a fresh singular visual or time referent without switching number.
course_items.not_yet: Systematic this/that/these/those contrast waits for A2.

course_items.title: Common adjective position and coordination
course_items.meaning_use: Describe familiar people, objects, homes, places, and weather with visible or known qualities.
course_items.mastery_evidence: Produce fresh noun and be descriptions with adjectives in the correct position.
course_items.not_yet: Comparison, adjective complements, and long adjective strings wait.

course_items.title: Very, really, and very much
course_items.meaning_use: Strengthen a basic description, preference, want, or fixed time expression.
course_items.mastery_evidence: Choose a licensed intensifier position in fresh descriptions and preference statements.
course_items.not_yet: Degree scales, downtoners, and intensifier-register choices wait.

course_items.title: Always and sometimes
course_items.meaning_use: Add a simple frequency to a familiar routine or repeated activity.
course_items.mastery_evidence: Place always or sometimes correctly in a fresh routine statement.
course_items.not_yet: Broader frequency scales and be-position control wait for extension.

course_items.title: Everything and something: limited chunks
course_items.meaning_use: Recognise and use a small number of high-utility indefinite references in fixed or transparent contexts.
course_items.mastery_evidence: Interpret fresh transparent examples and complete one familiar formula such as Everything is OK.
course_items.not_yet: The full some/any/no/every pronoun system waits for A2.

course_items.title: Basic place and relationship prepositions
exact_forms: place: in, on, at, under, near, next to, opposite
course_items.meaning_use: Locate people and things and express a simple destination or relationship.
course_items.mastery_evidence: Place fresh people or objects accurately in a pictured scene and interpret the same phrases.
course_items.not_yet: Finer spatial relations and idiomatic preposition choice wait.

course_items.title: Clock time, dates, and basic time placement
exact_forms: at + clock time; on + day/date; in + month/year/morning
day-month-year or month-day-year with ordinal dates
today, tomorrow, tomorrow morning, this evening, next week at clause end
course_items.meaning_use: Give and locate a basic event, meeting, schedule, or return time.
course_items.mastery_evidence: Transfer fresh spoken and written time/date information accurately across a schedule and message.
course_items.not_yet: Duration, deadlines, and complex calendar relations wait.

course_items.title: Here and there
exact_forms: here/there after be or a main verb
course_items.meaning_use: Refer economically to a place already visible, shared, or mentioned.
course_items.mastery_evidence: Use here or there to distinguish speaker-near and other location in a fresh scene.
course_items.not_yet: Broader deictic and directional adverbs wait.

course_items.title: And, but, and or
exact_forms: list items with and/or before the last item
omit the repeated second subject when it is unchanged
course_items.meaning_use: Add, contrast, choose, list, and connect two short related ideas.
course_items.mastery_evidence: Combine fresh short facts without losing the intended relation or subject.
course_items.not_yet: Discourse-level coordination and correlative conjunctions wait.

course_items.title: Because: one simple reason
exact_forms: main clause + because + subject + finite verb
course_items.meaning_use: Add one transparent reason after a simple statement, preference, or evaluation.
course_items.mastery_evidence: Join a fresh choice or feeling to one relevant reason with a complete because-clause.
course_items.not_yet: Fronted because-clauses and multi-clause reasoning wait.

course_items.title: Like, love, and want complements
course_items.meaning_use: Express a familiar preference or intended action with a bounded verb pattern.
course_items.mastery_evidence: Complete and produce fresh preference statements using one licensed complement pattern.
course_items.not_yet: Meaning contrasts among gerund and infinitive patterns wait.

course_items.title: Lexicalised verb-preposition patterns
course_items.meaning_use: Use a small taught set as whole patterns in routines, descriptions, needs, and interaction.
course_items.mastery_evidence: Choose the complete taught pattern in fresh transparent contexts without dropping its preposition.
course_items.not_yet: Productive phrasal-verb systems and free verb-preposition generalisation wait.

course_items.title: High-utility information question frames
exact_forms: What/Where/When/What time + do/does + subject + base verb?
How many + plural noun + are there?
course_items.meaning_use: Obtain the identity, place, time, price, or quantity needed in a predictable exchange.
course_items.mastery_evidence: Select and produce the frame that retrieves the missing detail in a fresh information gap.
course_items.not_yet: Why, which, whose, how long, and open-ended follow-up systems wait.

source_dispositions.source_label: ADJECTIVES > combining > FORM: COMBINING TWO ADJECTIVES WITH 'AND'
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use 'and' to join a limited range of common adjectives.
Can use 'very' with a limited range of common gradable adjectives.
Can use a limited range of adjectives attributively, before a noun. ► noun phrases
Can use a limited range of adjectives predicatively, after 'be'.
Can use the irregular superlative adjective 'best' in the phrase 'my best friend'.

source_dispositions.source_label: ADVERBS > adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings > USE: TIME
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use 'soon' in the phrases 'See you soon' and 'Get well soon', as a signing-off device.

source_dispositions.source_label: ADVERBS > adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings > USE: PLACE
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use a limited range of adverbs ('here', 'there') to indicate place.

source_dispositions.source_label: ADVERBS > adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings > USE: DEGREE WITH VERBS
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use 'really' and 'very much' with verbs expressing preference ('like', 'love'), for emphasis.

source_dispositions.source_label: ADVERBS > adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings > USE: 'VERY' WITH ADJECTIVES
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use 'very' to make adjectives stronger.

source_dispositions.source_label: ADVERBS > adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings > USE: FREQUENCY
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use a limited range of adverbs ('always', 'sometimes') to talk about frequency.

source_dispositions.source_label: ADVERBS > adverbs as modifiers > FORM: 'VERY' + ADJECTIVES
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use 'very' to modify common gradable adjectives.

source_dispositions.source_label: ADVERBS > adverbs as modifiers > FORM: 'VERY' + TIME ADVERBS
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use 'very' to modify time adverbs. ► adverb phrases

source_dispositions.source_label: ADVERBS > adverbs as modifiers > FORM: PLACE, COMPLEMENT
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use place adverbs ('here', 'there') as complements of verbs.

source_dispositions.source_label: ADVERBS > adverbs as modifiers > FORM: DEGREE and TIME, MODIFYING VERBS
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use degree and time adverbs to modify verbs.
Can use a limited range of adverbs in front position.

source_dispositions.source_label: ADVERBS > position > FORM: DEGREE, BEFORE ADJECTIVES
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use a limited range of degree adverbs before an adjective.

source_dispositions.source_label: ADVERBS > position > FORM: FREQUENCY, MID POSITION
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use frequency adverbs in the usual mid position, between the subject and the main verb.
Can use 'really' in the usual mid-position, between the subject and the main verb.

source_dispositions.source_label: ADVERBS > position > FORM: TIME, END POSITION
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use time adverbs in the usual end position.

source_dispositions.source_label: ADVERBS > position > FORM: PLACE, END POSITION
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use place adverbs in the usual end position.

source_dispositions.source_label: ADVERBS > adverb phrases - form > FORM: 'VERY' + ADVERB
source_dispositions.source_text: Can modify adverbs of time and degree with 'very'.

source_dispositions.source_label: CLAUSES > coordinated > FORM: CLAUSE + CLAUSE, ELLIPTED SUBJECT
source_dispositions.source_text: Can omit the subject in a second main declarative clause when the subject is obvious or the same as the first clause.

source_dispositions.source_label: CLAUSES > coordinated > FORM: MAIN CLAUSE + MAIN CLAUSE
source_dispositions.source_text: Can combine two main declarative clauses using co-ordinating conjunctions ('and', 'but', 'or').
Can form simple affirmative declarative clauses.

source_dispositions.source_label: CLAUSES > declarative > FORM: NEGATIVE DECLARATIVE WITH 'BE'
source_dispositions.source_text: Can form a simple negative declarative clause with lexical 'be' + 'not' or 'n't'.

source_dispositions.source_label: CLAUSES > declarative > FORM: NEGATIVE DECLARATIVE, LEXICAL VERBS
source_dispositions.source_text: Can form simple negative declarative clauses.

source_dispositions.source_label: CLAUSES > declarative > FORM: AFFIRMATIVE DECLARATIVE, MODAL AUXILIARY VERBS
source_dispositions.source_text: Can form an affirmative declarative clause with modal verbs.

source_dispositions.source_label: CLAUSES > interrogatives > FORM: AFFIRMATIVE INTERROGATIVE, WITH 'BE'
source_dispositions.source_text: Can form interrogative clauses with 'be'.
Can use a finite subordinate clause with 'because', after a main clause, to introduce reasons.
Can use single word conjunctions ('and, but, or') to combine phrases.
Can use single word conjunctions ('and, but, or') to combine sentences.
Can use 'and' and 'or' before the final item in a list.
Can use single word conjunctions ('and, but, or') to combine clauses.
Can use single word conjunctions ('and, but, or') to connect single nouns and adjectives.
Can use 'but' to add an unexpected contrast.
Can use 'because' as a subordinating conjunction to introduce a subordinate clause.
Can use articles 'the', 'a' and 'an' before nouns. ► noun phrases
Can use 'a' + 'very' + adjectives in basic noun phrases. ► adverbs ►  noun phrases
Can use 'a' and 'an' before adjectives in a noun phrase. ► adjectives ►  noun phrases
Can use 'the' in prepositional phrases relating to time.

source_dispositions.source_label: DETERMINERS > articles > FORM: PREPOSITION + NO ARTICLE
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use no article before a limited range of nouns in some fixed expressions with prepositions.
Can use no article before a limited range of singular, plural and uncountable nouns when referring to things in general.
Can use 'this' in a limited range of contexts to refer to places from the speaker's or writer's point of view. ► noun phrases ►  pronouns: demonstrative
Can use 'this' with time and date words to refer to 'the one that's coming'.

source_dispositions.source_label: DETERMINERS > demonstratives > FORM: 'THIS' WITH SINGULAR NOUNS
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use 'this' with singular nouns. ► noun phrases ►  pronouns: demonstrative
Can use possessive determiners 'my', 'your', 'his', 'her' and 'our' before nouns. ► noun phrases ► possessive pronouns

source_dispositions.source_label: DETERMINERS > quantity > FORM: WITH PLURAL NOUNS
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use a limited range of quantifying determiners with plural nouns ('some', 'lots of', 'a lot of' and numbers).

source_dispositions.source_label: DETERMINERS > quantity > FORM: WITH SINGULAR NOUNS
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use a limited range of quantifying determiners with singular nouns ('a', 'every').► determiners: articles

source_dispositions.source_label: FUTURE > future simple (with will and shall) > FORM: AFFIRMATIVE 'WILL'
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use the affirmative forms 'will' and ''ll'.

source_dispositions.source_label: FUTURE > future simple (with will and shall) > USE: PLANS AND INTENTIONS WITH 'WILL'
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use 'will' and ''ll' to talk about plans and intentions.
Can use the affirmative form.
Can use the affirmative question form.
Can use the negative forms.
Can use 'can' to make an offer.
Can use 'can' to talk about ability to do something.
Can use 'can' to make a request.
Can use 'can' to talk about possibility.
Can use the affirmative forms.

source_dispositions.source_label: MODALITY > will > USE: PLANS AND INTENTIONS
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use 'will' to talk about plans and intentions.
Can use 'would like to invite' to make invitations.
Can use the affirmative form with 'like'.

source_dispositions.source_label: MODALITY > would > USE: WISHES AND PREFERENCES WITH 'LIKE'
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use 'would like' to talk about wishes and preferences.

source_dispositions.source_label: NEGATION > negation > FORM: AUXILIARY VERB 'DO', PRESENT
source_dispositions.source_text: Can form negative statements of main verbs in the present simple with 'don't' + main verb. ► present simple ► can
Can form negative statements of main verb 'be', with contracted and uncontracted forms.
Can use negative form 'can’t'.

source_dispositions.source_label: NOUNS > noun phrases > FORM: ADJECTIVE + PLURAL NOUN
source_dispositions.source_text: Can form simple noun phrases by pre-modifying plural nouns with an adjective and no determiner.

source_dispositions.source_label: NOUNS > noun phrases > FORM: DETERMINER + ADJECTIVE + NOUN
source_dispositions.source_text: Can form simple noun phrases by pre-modifying singular and plural nouns with an adjective after a determiner.

source_dispositions.source_label: NOUNS > noun phrases > FORM: DETERMINER + NOUN
source_dispositions.source_text: Can form simple noun phrases with a limited range of determiners + singular and plural nouns. ► Nouns and noun phrases: functions

source_dispositions.source_label: NOUNS > noun phrases > FORM: NOUN + NOUN
source_dispositions.source_text: Can form noun phrases by pre-modifying a limited range of nouns with another noun.
Can use proper nouns with a capital letter to refer to specific people, places, days and things.
Can use a limited range of common nouns.
Can use a range of compound nouns, as one-word, two-word and hyphenated compounds, formed from verb + noun, noun + noun and adjective + noun combinations.
Can form plurals by adding '-s' to common countable nouns.

source_dispositions.source_label: NOUNS > noun phrases - grammatical functions > FORM: AS SUBJECTS
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use nouns and noun phrases as subjects of the clause.

source_dispositions.source_label: NOUNS > noun phrases - grammatical functions > FORM: AS COMPLEMENT OF PREPOSITIONS
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use nouns and noun phrases as complements of prepositions in prepositional phrases.

source_dispositions.source_label: NOUNS > noun phrases - grammatical functions > FORM: AS OBJECTS
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use nouns and noun phrases as objects of the clause.

source_dispositions.source_label: NOUNS > noun phrases - grammatical functions > FORM: AS ADJUNCTS
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use nouns and noun phrases as adjuncts in some time expressions.

source_dispositions.source_label: NOUNS > noun phrases - grammatical functions > FORM: AS COMPLEMENT OF 'BE'
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use nouns and noun phrases as complements of the verb 'be'.
Can use the affirmative form with a limited range of regular and irregular verbs.

source_dispositions.source_label: PAST > past simple > USE: EVERYDAY EVENTS AND STATES
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use the past simple to talk about everyday events or states.

source_dispositions.source_label: PREPOSITIONS > prepostions > FORM: PREPOSITION + NOUN PHRASE
source_dispositions.source_text: Can form prepositional phrases with a preposition and a noun phrase.
Can use a limited range of simple (single-word) prepositions.
Can use the affirmative form.

source_dispositions.source_label: PRESENT > present continuous > USE: EVENTS IN PROGRESS
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use the present continuous with a limited range of verbs to talk about situations and events in progress.
Can use the negative form with a limited range of regular and irregular verbs.

source_dispositions.source_label: PRESENT > present simple > USE: HABITS AND GENERAL FACTS
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use the present simple to talk about repeated events or habits, and general facts.
Can use the affirmative form with a limited range of regular and irregular verbs.
Can use the present simple with the adverb 'really' as an intensifier. ► adverbs

source_dispositions.source_label: PRONOUNS > subject/ object > FORM: (SUBJECT) QUESTIONS WITH 'BE'
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use the pronouns 'you' and 'it' after 'be' in question forms.
Can use the pronoun 'it' as a direct object to refer to an object or situation already referred to.

source_dispositions.source_label: PRONOUNS > subject/ object > FORM: (OBJECT) WITH PREPOSITION
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use the object pronouns 'me', 'you', 'him', 'her', 'it', 'us' and 'them' in the object position after prepositions.
Can use the pronouns 'I', 'you', 'we' and 'they' after an auxiliary or modal verb in question forms.
Can use the pronouns 'me', 'you', 'him', 'her', 'us' and 'them' in the direct object position after a transitive verb.

source_dispositions.source_label: PRONOUNS > subject/ object > FORM: (SUBJECT) 'IT' FOR FIRST PERSON
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use the pronoun 'it' before 'be' to refer to a first person speaker or writer.
Can use the pronouns 'I', 'you', 'he', 'she', 'it', 'we' and 'they' in the subject position before a verb in statements.

source_dispositions.source_label: PRONOUNS > indefinite - thing, -one, -body etc > FORM: OBJECT
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use a limited range of indefinite pronouns as objects.

source_dispositions.source_label: PRONOUNS > indefinite - thing, -one, -body etc > FORM: 'EVERYTHING', SUBJECT
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use 'everything' as subject, with a singular verb.
Can use a limited range of modal verbs + subject + main verb to form 'yes/no' questions.  ► can

source_dispositions.source_label: VERBS > prepositional > FORM: VERB + PREPOSITION + OBJECT
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use a limited range of prepositional verbs followed by noun or pronoun objects.
Can use auxiliary verb 'be'. ►  present continuous

source_dispositions.source_label: VERBS > types > FORM: MODAL AUXILIARY VERBS
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use a limited range of modal auxiliary verbs ('can', 'will', 'would').
Can use linking verb 'be'.
Can use regular and irregular main verbs in simple verb phrases. ► present simple ► past simple

source_dispositions.source_label: VERBS > patterns_with to and -ing > FORM: VERB + 'TO'-INFINITIVE
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use a limited range of verbs followed by a 'to'- infinitive.

source_dispositions.source_label: VERBS > patterns_with to and -ing > FORM: 'WOULD LIKE TO'
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use 'would like to' + infinitive.

source_dispositions.source_label: VERBS > patterns_with to and -ing > FORM: 'LIKE' + 'TO'-INFINITIVE OR + '-ING'
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use 'like' followed either by a 'to'-infinitive or an '-ing' form, with no change in meaning.
Can use 'there is' + singular noun phrase as complement.
Can use 'there are' + plural noun phrase as complement.
Can use linking verb 'be' with complements.
Can ask basic questions using ‘What’s your ...?’

source_dispositions.source_label: GSE 24: agreement between nouns and verb ‘be’
source_dispositions.source_text: Can use the correct form of ‘be’ with singular and plural nouns.

source_dispositions.source_label: GSE 24: statements with subject + verb + object
source_dispositions.source_text: Can make basic statements with subject + verb + object.
